static_findings.snippet: - Always use strict mode with `set -Eeuo pipefail` and proper error trapping
- Prefer arrays and proper iteration over unsafe patterns like `for f in $(ls)`
- Use `[[ ]]` for Bash conditionals, fall back to `[ ]` for POSIX compliance
- Implement comprehensive argument parsing with `getopts` and usage functions
- Create temporary files and directories safely with `mktemp` and cleanup traps
- Prefer `printf` over `echo` for predictable output formatting
- Use command substitution `$()` instead of backticks for readability
- Use `shopt -s inherit_errexit` for better error propagation in Bash 4.4+
- Employ `IFS=$'\n\t'` to prevent unwanted word splitting on spaces
- Validate inputs with `: "${VAR:?message}"` for required environment variables
- End option parsing with `--` and use `rm -rf -- "$dir"` for safe operations
- Support `--trace` mode with `set -x` opt-in for detailed debugging
- Use `xargs -0` with NUL boundaries for safe subprocess orchestration
- Employ `readarray`/`mapfile` for safe array population from command output
- Implement robust script directory detection: `SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
- Use NUL-safe patterns: `find -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do ...; done`
- Use `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang for portability across systems
- Check Bash version at script start: `(( BASH_VERSINFO[0] >= 4 && BASH_VERSINFO[1] >= 4 ))` for Bas
- Validate required external commands exist: `command -v jq &>/dev/null || exit 1`
- Detect platform differences: `case "$(uname -s)" in Linux*) ... ;; Darwin*) ... ;; esac`
- Handle GNU vs BSD tool differences (e.g., `sed -i` vs `sed -i ''`)
- Use long-form options in scripts for clarity: `--verbose` instead of `-v`
- Use descriptive function names that explain purpose: `validate_input_file` not `check_file`
- Place opening braces on same line for consistency: `function_name() {`
- Declare constants with `readonly` to prevent accidental modification
- Use `local` keyword for all function variables to avoid polluting global scope
- Implement `timeout` for external commands: `timeout 30s curl ...` prevents hangs
- Validate file permissions before operations: `[[ -r "$file" ]] || exit 1`
- Use process substitution `<(command)` instead of temporary files when possible
- Validate numeric input with pattern matching: `[[ $num =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]`
- Never use `eval` on user input; use arrays for dynamic command construction
- Set restrictive umask for sensitive operations: `(umask 077; touch "$secure_file")`
- Use `--` to separate options from arguments: `rm -rf -- "$user_input"`
- Validate environment variables before using: `: "${REQUIRED_VAR:?not set}"`
- Use `trap` to ensure cleanup happens even on abnormal exit
- Avoid subshells in loops; use `while read` instead of `for i in $(cat file)`
- Use Bash built-ins over external commands: `[[ ]]` instead of `test`, `${var//pattern/replacement}

- Use arithmetic expansion `$(( ))` instead of `expr` for calculations

content.value_statement: Bash automation often fails under unusual inputs, platform differences, or partial errors. This skill provides defensive patterns for safer scripts, tests, linting, and CI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Designs Bash scripts with strict mode, traps, safe quoting, and input validation.
Reviews shell scripts for unsafe expansion, fragile parsing, missing cleanup, and portability risks.
Creates argument parsing, usage output, logging, and dry-run behavior for automation scripts.
Recommends ShellCheck, shfmt, Bats, shellspec, and CI checks for Bash projects.
Explains Bash 4.4 and 5.x features, including arrays, mapfile, traps, and parameter expansion.
Plans temporary file handling, dependency checks, and platform-specific fallbacks.
limitations: It focuses on Bash and does not replace a higher-level language for complex applications.
It does not execute, lint, or test scripts unless the host agent runs separate tools.
It is not a POSIX-only shell guide and may use Bash-specific features.
Generated scripts still need review in the target operating system and CI environment.

use_cases.title: Create CI Automation Scripts
use_cases.description: Generate reliable Bash scripts for build, test, release, and deployment jobs with clear failure handling.

use_cases.title: Review Operations Utilities
use_cases.description: Audit internal shell utilities for quoting errors, unsafe cleanup, missing validation, and portability problems.

use_cases.title: Modernize Legacy Shell Code
use_cases.description: Refactor older Bash scripts toward clearer functions, safer arrays, test coverage, and documented dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Safe Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Bash script for [task]. Include strict mode, safe argument parsing, input validation, cleanup traps, and usage output.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Bash
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Bash script for safety, portability, quoting, error handling, cleanup, and ShellCheck issues. Suggest specific fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Tests and CI
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a test and CI plan for this Bash project using Bats or shellspec, ShellCheck, shfmt, and platform matrix testing.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Production Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Harden this Bash automation workflow for production. Address privilege boundaries, dry-run behavior, dependency checks, logging, rollback, and observability.

output_examples.input: A request to write a file cleanup script for CI workspaces.
output_examples.output: A script plan with validated paths, dry-run mode, safe deletion boundaries, cleanup traps, and clear usage text.

output_examples.input: A legacy Bash deployment script that fails intermittently.
output_examples.output: A review summary covering quoting, unchecked commands, fragile subshells, missing traps, and recommended test cases.

output_examples.input: A team needs repeatable shell quality checks in CI.
output_examples.output: A CI checklist using ShellCheck, shfmt, Bats, actionlint, version matrix testing, and release gate recommendations.

best_practices: State inputs, outputs, side effects, and failure modes before generating a script.
Ask for tests, linting, dry-run support, and safe cleanup behavior for production scripts.
Review generated commands against the target environment before running them.
anti_patterns: Using generated scripts directly on production systems without review and dry-run testing.
Requesting complex application logic in Bash when another language would be safer.
Ignoring platform differences between Linux, macOS, BSD tools, and CI containers.

faq.question: Does this skill write complete Bash scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft scripts with argument parsing, logging, cleanup, validation, and defensive error handling.

faq.question: Can it review an existing shell script?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the script and ask for findings about safety, portability, readability, tests, and CI readiness.

faq.question: Does it support POSIX sh?
faq.answer: Only partially. The skill focuses on Bash and may recommend Bash-specific features when they improve safety or clarity.

faq.question: Which tools does it recommend?
faq.answer: It commonly recommends ShellCheck, shfmt, Bats, shellspec, actionlint, Semgrep, gitleaks, and related CI checks.

faq.question: Will it run generated commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill is guidance for script creation and review. Any execution depends on the host agent and user approval.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that generate or review Bash automation.
